title: Cancer risk of pro-regenerative anti-aging interventions
bottleneck: Every powerful rejuvenation lever (telomerase activation, Yamanaka reprogramming, stem cell expansion, growth-factor signaling) overlaps mechanistically with cancer: the same pathways that restore youthful proliferation can immortalize a precancerous cell. The field has no general framework for rejuvenating tissues without increasing malignancy risk.
why_it_blocks: Cancer is already the leading cause of death in the 'successfully aged.' If anti-aging therapies trade one aging disease for more cancer, they fail the fundamental test of extending healthy life.
current_state: This tradeoff is managed case-by-case (e.g., cyclical reprogramming to avoid tumors) rather than solved. Long-term cancer surveillance data from any human rejuvenation trial do not yet exist. Progeroid mouse models tolerate reprogramming better than wild-type animals, hinting the cancer-rejuvenation tradeoff may depend on baseline damage burden, but this is untested in humans.
